evidence:
Scope and authority: read the actual frozen root XLSX and bundled XLSX with openpyxl, Quality Checks row 19 (number 18) and Internal Quality Checks row 19. Both say, "The reference plausibly satisfies every criterion the judges score, so the oracle can score high." The Internal row has no added annotation/comment. Applied frozen Harbor SKILL.md and references/quality-checks.md:18 (walk every criterion; an impossible reference criterion is P0), staged runtime/criterion contract, deterministic solve/prompt/schema guidance, and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. This verdict is about plausible reference coverage, not an asserted Oracle reward.

Inventory: parsed every current judge.toml: Render 1, Constraints 1, Functional 64, Polish 7, Visual 6 = 79 criteria. Read all five prompts and app_context, including the exact fixtures in Functional S01-S24/S34/S36. No current criterion was found without a plausible reference implementation. The complete criterion inventory inspected is appended below.

Binding and raw evidence: independently SHA256-checked RESULTS.json against raw-evidence-index.json: ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09. All 22 actual_app_files match the frozen solution/app bytes, including the built frontend; the frozen Functional judge and prompt hashes match, and every copied driver matches RESULTS.driver_sha256. The raw report records no missing or failed expected functional fact keys. I inspected the executed run_workflow, workflow_core, workspace, runtime, current, library, boundary, repair and surface driver code and the underlying observations rather than accepting those booleans alone. RESULTS.json:actual_app_files, facts, pre/post and surface are the cited raw sections.

Reference coverage: solution/app/src/app.tsx:53 openExample, :62 save and :142 startup support S01; the built-in hello.js produces squares 1 through 144 and console output. Raw S01 observations show automatic startup without Run, authored output, and a separately saved exact edited copy while the original example remains unchanged. Runtime.ts:7 instrument, :47 sandboxBootstrap, buildRun, and :232 PreviewRunner implement case-insensitive filename dispatch; fresh JS/HTML contexts; CSS preservation of content/prior style without scripts or handlers; lifecycle cancellation and rollback; origin/network boundaries; unsupported-family refusal; timed literal loops/callbacks; and source-line error reporting/recovery. Raw S02 CSS retained background rgb(1, 2, 3), applied red text, and held script/handler counts at 1 before/after the enabled button click. S03 recorded click/key/input after 6104.75/6103.31 ms idle periods and unchanged counts after Stop. S04 recorded a successful four-second callback/error before proving cancellation, and Stop restored run-B-undefined. S09 finite controls actually returned 3, 4, 3; the three infinite-loop trials terminated in 4997.79, 5010.06 and 4989.70 ms, each retaining timeout-control. S10-S13 new log entries report forEeach line 4, undefinedFunctionCall line 6, timer errors lines 2/6, and Error/plain-string promise rejection lines 2/2/6, with respective last-good bodies and later recovery markers. S36 records the working nested control and outer callback entry with no forbidden nested completion after the full window. S05 reports four blocked parent operations with unchanged storage; S07's successful text/image transport controls yield delivery baseline 2, and both authored refusals leave deliveries at 2 with ordinary recovery.

Console/editor/theme: app.tsx:16 Value recursively exposes nested objects/arrays, the log handler appends level-labelled entries, and clear removes them. Raw S14 has log/warn/error/info in positions 3/4/5/6 with Complete status; S15 shows tag/object-check, nested/deep/nested-value and individual array values 11/22/33. S16 records successful short/delayed durations 5.8/4001.3 ms, measured delayed lifetime 4085.12 ms, plus failed/Stop/timeout durations and history/Clear observations. app.tsx:134 debounces source/filename edits with cleanup on Auto-run changes; S17 measures 559.05 ms automatic execution, closer-spaced continued edits with no intermediate markers, 3000 ms off/queue windows and actual manual execution of the same idle sources. app.tsx:126-133 initializes CodeMirror, language/theme compartments and named editor; S19 observed equal narrow/wide text width 52, actual gutter numbers 1 and 2, and multiple token colours for all three languages. S34 measured actual chrome/editor/console changes through two theme toggles while exact fields/output remained intact.

Persistence: server.js:41 fields trims titles, :52 matchingRevision refuses stale revisions, :60 uniqueTitle uses case-sensitive equality, and POST/PUT transactions preserve identity and increment revisions. server.js:113 opens the DB_PATH SQLite file with an idempotent schema. app.tsx save retains dirty fields on error and exposes conflict/reload recovery. Raw S21/S22 observes exact separate records through reload and actual process restart, then a successful current-revision write with unrelated records unchanged. actual-restart.json records exactly one call, PID 16 to 338; launch_workflow.py also waits for the old process to exit. The separate inherited-restart counterexample is a harness weakness on a different app, not evidence that this reference cannot satisfy S22. Raw S23 has two actual dirty editors, unchanged winners on HTTP 409, retained exact dirty fields, and successful recovery revisions 3 and 5 on the same identity 7. S24 shows title trimming on create/update, unchanged records for exact/padded/empty/whitespace collision attempts, valid recovery and coexisting case-distinct identities. The S21 execution canary keeps monitor revision 3 unchanged through save/update/load and five seconds, then the exact successful positive control changes it to revision 4. This is bounded text-storage evidence, not a universal proof of no server evaluation.

Gates, Polish and Visual: source and raw surface checks support authored preview/console execution and independent clean-context save/load/reload. surface_flow.cjs uses actual keyboard events for its library route and records all 11 requested control purposes reached with visible 2px focus outlines; it then edits/runs on a 390x844 viewport and clears the console. app.tsx renders named editor, preview, console and saved-library controls; style.css provides responsive stacking, readable panes and both themes. I viewed desktop-theme-one.png, desktop-theme-two.png and mobile.png from the supplemental surface capture. The captures show coherent consistent controls, separated labelled panels, readable contrasting text and logical stacked mobile composition, plausibly satisfying all six permissive five-anchor visual criteria. A blank off-viewport iframe area in the full-page mobile capture is not treated as failed execution; direct mobile execution/clear evidence is separate, and Visual grades the playground chrome.

Alternative/broken-app challenge: a conventional single-column/native-control implementation, an initially light theme, or a static last-good snapshot after Stop remains conforming under the actual prompts and anchors; none is being imposed as a hidden reference requirement. An implementation that refuses every loop, never executes timers, or silently discards dirty fields cannot borrow credit from absent output: the current S09 finite controls, S04/S36 positive callbacks, and two S23 dirty-editor observations discriminate those failures. These challenges revealed no row-18 false-pass/false-fail witness requiring a task change.

Limit: these are source and direct scripted-browser observations. RESULTS.json explicitly says oracle_score_claimed=false; surface-results.json says visual_grade_measured=false. No full configured LLM judge/Oracle/target-builder reward or measured LLM workload was supplied. They remain unmeasured and are not upgraded to a score claim; their required clearance belongs to the separate runtime/reward checks. No reference-coverage defect is confirmed by the supplied evidence.
